clue.text: Cook's vessel? Yes and no

parts.note: a pan in which a cook prepares vegetables by vapour is one sense, but Captain Cook sailed under canvas, never on a ship driven by an engine, hence yes and no

explanation.surface: A question about Captain Cook's ship, answered both ways at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital C hides the kitchen cook behind the explorer: the kitchen pot fits, the explorer's sailing ship does not.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen vessel for cooking food in vapour, and also a ship powered by an engine, which Captain Cook never had.

clue.text: Cut around page that is intertwined

indicators.note: around means the word for cut goes round the page letter

parts.note: sliced means cut

explanation.surface: A slice taken round a page that is woven in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' is only a link here, not IE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ropes or film joined by weaving or overlapping their ends together are joined in this way.

clue.text: Lengthy repairs to Exit Seven

indicators.note: repairs to suggests the letters of Exit Seven are fixed up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Roadworks at a motorway junction that drag on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wide-ranging or large in extent can also be long-drawn-out.

clue.text: Fruit gives person energy

parts.note: man means a person
go means energy, get-up-and-go

explanation.surface: Eating fruit gives you pep.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical stone fruit with sweet orange flesh.

clue.text: Check exercise in relaxation

indicators.note: in means the word for exercise sits inside the word for relaxation

parts.note: rest means relaxation
to train is to exercise

explanation.surface: Doing a workout while trying to relax.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding back or curbing something is a restriction on it.

clue.text: One of Bill's victims in port of New York

definitions.meaning: ... Bill Cody, the American showman and hunter, shot thousands of bison
a city on Lake Erie in New York State

explanation.definitionFit: The bison slaughtered by Buffalo Bill share their name with the lake port city in New York State.

clue.text: Show fault in endless trust

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the word for trust is cut off

parts.note: belief means trust or faith

explanation.surface: Revealing a flaw in faith that never ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To contradict or show something to be false is to expose a flaw in it.

clue.text: Fare on train revealing natural hierarchy

parts.note: fare means food
a train is a chain or series of things

explanation.surface: The food served on a railway journey tells you about rank.
explanation.definitionFit: The order in which creatures eat one another forms a ranked sequence in nature.

clue.text: This walk, between two rivers, would do for walker

indicators.note: between says the answer sits inside the two rivers, so removing them from the word for walker leaves it

parts.note: a rambler is a walker in the countryside
R is an abbreviation for river, so two of them give two Rs

explanation.surface: A stroll between two rivers would suit a hiker.
explanation.walkthrough: Put the answer between R and R and it would do for (become) a word for walker; 'would do for' joins the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A leisurely, unhurried stroll.

clue.text: Nothing deters fluctuation in magnetic measurement

parts.note: O is the figure nought, nothing

indicators.note: fluctuation in means the letters of deters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: Zero discourages changes in a magnetic reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit in the old centimetre-gram-second system for magnetic field strength, named after a Danish physicist.

clue.text: As used by Virgil, at inordinate length?

definitions.text: As used by Virgil, at inordinate length?

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark that the Roman poet went on far too long.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'length' as the definition, but the answer names no length: it is the language Virgil wrote in, so the whole clue defines it while 'used by' points to the letters inside 'Virgil, at inordinate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgil, the Roman poet of the Aeneid, wrote in the ancient tongue of Rome.

clue.text: Quickly stop a learner entering the lounge

indicators.note: entering means the a and learner letters go inside the word for quickly

parts.note: soon means quickly, before long
L is the learner driver's plate
to bar is to stop or block

explanation.surface: Telling a driving pupil to hurry up and stop before going into the lounge.
explanation.walkthrough: A SALOON BAR is the more comfortable lounge room of a traditional British pub.
explanation.definitionFit: In a British pub the plusher room, with carpets and higher prices, is called the lounge or the saloon.

clue.text: Coming together to study with classes

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a course is a series of classes

explanation.surface: Meeting up to study alongside lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering or convergence of people or things in one place is a confluence of them.

clue.text: Painter might go round this class and scoff

parts.note: CL is an abbreviation for class
to scoff is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: An artist walks around the classroom and gobbles food.
explanation.walkthrough: A painter here is the rope at a small boat's bow, made fast by winding it round a metal fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat's mooring rope, called a painter, is tied off around this fitting with two horns.

clue.text: Stoop to hear foreigner

indicators.note: to hear says the word for foreigner is taken by its sound and then spelt differently

parts.note: a Dane, from Denmark, is a foreigner to a British setter

explanation.surface: Bending down to listen to a visitor from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: To condescend to do something beneath one is to stoop to it.

clue.text: Sick aunt has to get better, of course

indicators.note: sick means unwell, so the letters of aunt are disordered

parts.note: to rally is to recover, to get better

explanation.surface: An ill aunt has to recover, obviously.
explanation.definitionFit: As an interjection meaning certainly or obviously, it is a synonym for of course.

clue.text: Deeply impressed in reading novel

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the letters of in reading are given a new order

explanation.surface: Someone moved deeply by the book they are reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fixed firmly in the mind or character is deep-rooted, as if worked into the fibre.

clue.text: Rabelaisian character (with name for being enormous)

definitions.text: Rabelaisian character (with name for being enormous)

parts.words: Rabelaisian character (with name for being enormous)
parts.note: a giant in the comic novels of Rabelais whose name, with N added, became an adjective meaning huge

explanation.surface: A figure from Rabelais, famous for being gigantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with name' hints that adding N, the abbreviation for name, turns the giant's name into a word for enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant hero of Rabelais's sixteenth-century French comic novels, father of Pantagruel.

clue.text: Points to stall as place for daily provision

parts.note: N, E, W and S are the four compass points
a stand is a stall

explanation.surface: Directions to a market stall that sells something every day.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiosk selling the daily papers supplies readers each morning.

clue.text: Publication like The Observer?

parts.note: a weekly British magazine of politics, like the newspaper named for someone who watches; the name itself means one who looks on

explanation.surface: Asking about a periodical similar to a well-known Sunday newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper; the answer is a British weekly magazine whose name also means an onlooker.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running British weekly magazine, and also a word for an onlooker or watcher at an event.

clue.text: Celebrated ram made to get to work

parts.note: star means celebrated, as in a star player
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A famous ram is forced to go to work.
explanation.definitionFit: To set going or begin operating, as an engine or business is set going.

clue.text: Powerful Indian's catch secures a wicket

definitions.note: the possessive 's reads as is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: secures means the word for catch holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: to nab is to catch
W is the cricket scoreboard abbreviation for a wicket

explanation.surface: A mighty Indian's catch on the cricket field takes a wicket.
explanation.walkthrough: The A W sits after the first letter of NAB.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mughal provincial governor or viceroy in India, later a title for a Muslim nobleman of rank.

clue.text: Appropriate timber for a spar?

parts.note: a spar is a boat's pole, but also a practice bout in the ring, and this hard wood has a name fit for fighting

explanation.surface: Asking which wood suits a ship's mast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spar' looks like a ship's pole; read it as sparring, practice fighting, and the wood's name starts with the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A dense, fine-grained hard wood from an evergreen shrub, its name beginning with the word for prize fighting.

clue.text: Hedda losing her head? Not as weak as that

indicators.note: losing her head means the first letter of her surname is dropped

parts.note: Hedda Gabler is the title heroine of Ibsen's play

explanation.surface: Ibsen's heroine going mad, and wondering if she is stronger for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Hedda Gabler is the doomed heroine of Henrik Ibsen's play; without its first letter G her surname leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: More capable or competent is the comparative of able, the opposite of weaker.

clue.text: Credulously take a worthless purchase, under a pound

indicators.note: under means, in a down entry, the following pieces go below the pound letter

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from Latin libra
to be sold a pup is to buy something worthless

explanation.surface: Being gullible enough to buy a dud for less than a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sold a pup' is a British idiom for being cheated with a worthless buy.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept something eagerly and without question, like a cat drinking cream.

clue.text: Poor. Gaelic, unknown women, supposedly

parts.note: weak means poor, of low quality
Erse is an old name for Scottish or Irish Gaelic
X is the algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A list of deprived groups: the poor, Gaelic speakers, the unknown, and women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supposedly' marks the old phrase as a prejudice, not a fact.
explanation.definitionFit: An old patronising phrase for the female sex, implying they lack physical strength.

clue.text: Carried on receiving pay

definitions.meaning: one carries on or conducts a war or campaign
paid a salary, as in salaried work

explanation.definitionFit: A war is conducted or carried on, and salaried employment is paid work.

clue.text: Throw out Peel's reform without vote

indicators.note: without means outside, so the rearranged letters go round the vote mark
reform means the letters of Peel are formed again in a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
X is the cross marked on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: Rejecting Robert Peel's reforms without a ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' turns PEEL into EPEL, which goes round X. Sir Robert Peel was a nineteenth-century British prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject or force someone to leave is to throw them out.

clue.text: It's used finally to make attic outstanding

definitions.text: It's used finally to make attic
definitions.meaning: the last set of stairs a climber takes on the way up to the roof space

explanation.definitionFit: The highest set of stairs leads to the roof space, and the phrase also means excellent or first-class.

clue.text: Good with an old instrument

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means good

explanation.surface: Something good accompanied by an antique musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard musical instrument whose strings are struck by hammers.

clue.text: Visibly astonished as father gets inspected

parts.note: pop is a familiar word for father
eyed means looked over, inspected

explanation.surface: Dad is examined and looks startled.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone amazed has eyes wide open and bulging, so the surprise shows on the face.

clue.text: Used references from a thick back edition

indicators.note: back means the word for thick is written in reverse order

parts.note: thick means dull, slow-witted

explanation.surface: Quoting sources from the reverse of a fat volume.
explanation.definitionFit: To mention something indirectly is to make a passing reference to it.
